module_title: Gallantry Awards - Institutional History, Evolution, and Landmark Heroes
introduction: This level reviews the exact timeline of the establishment of these awards, the historical change in nomenclature for peacetime medals, and iconic modern heroes whose acts of bravery are frequently questioned in competitive exams.

core_concepts.title: Establishment Timeline (January 26, 1950)
core_concepts.description: Post-independence, the first three wartime gallantry awards (Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra) were officially instituted by the Government of India on January 26, 1950. However, they were given retrospective effect from August 15, 1947.

core_concepts.title: Evolution of Peacetime Award Names
core_concepts.description: On January 4, 1952, the government introduced the peacetime medals under a unified name: 'Ashoka Chakra'. It was split into three tiers: Class I, Class II, and Class III. On January 27, 1967, these were officially renamed Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra respectively.

core_concepts.title: Maha Vir Chakra (MVC) and Vir Chakra (VrC)
core_concepts.description: The Maha Vir Chakra is the second-highest wartime decoration, followed by the Vir Chakra. These medals recognize conspicuous gallantry on land, at sea, or in the air.

core_concepts.title: Kirti Chakra and Shaurya Chakra
core_concepts.description: The peacetime equivalents to the MVC and VrC. The Kirti Chakra is the second-highest peacetime gallantry award, while the Shaurya Chakra serves as the third-highest.

important_entities.name: Captain Vikram Batra
important_entities.significance: The legendary icon of the 1999 Kargil War whose battlefield victory cry 'Yeh Dil Maange More!' became a national sensation during the capture of Point 5140 and Point 4875.

important_entities.name: Neerja Bhanot
important_entities.significance: A flight purser who sacrificed her life saving passengers during the hijacking of Pan Am Flight 73 in Karachi in 1986. She remains the youngest and the first female recipient of the Ashoka Chakra.

important_entities.name: Group Captain Abhinandan Varthaman
important_entities.significance: Awarded for shooting down a Pakistani F-16 fighter jet during an aerial dogfight following the Balakot airstrike, demonstrating exceptional composure while under captivity.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Unlike civilian honors like the initial rules of the Bharat Ratna, all six gallantry awards were designed from day one to be fully open to posthumous (after death) nominations. A significant majority of Param Vir Chakras and Ashoka Chakras have been awarded posthumously.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Ashoka (Ashoka Chakra - 1st) -> Kirti (Kirti Chakra - 2nd) -> Shaurya (Shaurya Chakra - 3rd).

exam_strategy_tips: Questions testing the original names of these awards are highly popular in SSC CGL and State PCS. Remember that before 1967, Shaurya Chakra was known as 'Ashoka Chakra, Class III'.
